findings.description: The Yale Budget Lab citation (550K jobs) describes tariff-driven job losses, but the surrounding text pivots to 'Workers facing AI-driven unemployment' — adjacency creates an implication that the 550K figure represents AI displacement. The template-letters version correctly attributes to 'trade policy changes.'
findings.suggestion: Mirror the template-letters framing: attribute the 550K figure explicitly to trade policy, then note that AI displacement compounds the picture separately. Example: 'Trade policy changes project a loss of 550,000 jobs (Yale Budget Lab). AI-driven displacement adds to this pressure — without a government strategy to manage either transition, workers face compounding risks.'
findings.context: A [projected loss of 550,000 jobs](https://budgetlab.yale.edu/research/state-us-tariffs-february-20-2026) (Yale Budget Lab) — without a government strategy to absorb the displacement — should alarm every constituent. Workers facing AI-driven unemployment deserve more than policy silence.

findings.description: The corrected text now acknowledges 1979 hearings ('held hearings in 1979 but never advanced the treaty') but the next sentence retains '49-year absence of democratic deliberation.' Hearings constitute democratic deliberation — the characterization contradicts the correction.
findings.suggestion: Replace 'absence of democratic deliberation' with a more precise characterization. Options: '47-year gap since the last committee action' or '49 years without a committee vote or floor vote' — both acknowledge the hearings while capturing the genuine absence of advancement.
findings.context: The United States signed the ICESCR in 1977. The Senate Foreign Relations Committee held hearings in 1979 but never advanced the treaty to a committee vote or floor vote. That gap represents a 49-year absence of democratic deliberation on a question the empirical literature now treats as consequential.

findings.description: The $990B Medicaid cut and 10M coverage loss claims appear without inline source citation. The glossary entry for OBBBA attributes these figures to KFF (gross/net) and CBO (coverage), but the talking point does not link to either source or to the glossary entry.
findings.suggestion: Add inline attribution matching the pattern used for the Article 6 talking point. Example: 'approximately $990B (gross; ~$911B net, [KFF](https://www.kff.org/...)) from Medicaid — approximately 10M lost coverage ([CBO](https://www.cbo.gov/...)).' Alternatively, link to the glossary entry: '[OBBBA](/glossary#obbba) cut approximately $990B...'
findings.context: The OBBBA cut approximately $990B (gross; ~$911B net) from Medicaid — approximately 10M lost coverage through a single legislative action.

payload.notes: The changes under review improve quality — adding Yale Budget Lab and EPI citation links, and correcting a factual error that previously claimed the treaty never received committee hearings. Finding f2 represents a residual inconsistency from the correction process (the claim language did not fully update to match the new factual framing).

epistemic_flags: f1 confidence 0.80 — the adjacency inference depends on reader interpretation; some readers may not conflate the tariff and AI claims
f3 confidence 0.75 — the glossary carries attribution; whether point-of-use citation adds value depends on site conventions for talking points vs. analytical pages
